open_items.text: SAFETY LANE QUESTION, not actionable here: iter_encoded_sensitive scans each base64 RUN separately, so a 76-column fixture is read as 57-byte windows and a structural rule whose quieting marker sits outside the window fires on a clean file. Measured on NAME_FIELD. The standalone_slot fixture sidesteps it by keeping 32-character decorations; nothing fixes it for a shorter one

MEASURED: a committed base64 blob encoding 24 consecutive zero bytes contains a 32-character run of 'A', which is a hex run and a PRODUCTUSERID finding on the file TEXT. Guarded by test_no_fixture_encodes_a_long_run_of_zero_bytes; the builder authors the payload. Any future save fixture with a zeroed native struct meets this

standalone_slot.gvas.b64 is 19867 raw bytes rather than the under-10-KB target. 12972 of them are tag overhead (5046 names, 7311 recursive type names, 615 size and flag fields over 123 properties) and the type names are the game's own struct identities. Reaching 10 KB means dropping a container the brief asked to keep - reopen only with a decision about which shape to lose
